subject: MSA / Order Form - proposal on liability cap and carve-outs
messages:
From: Amelia Cho <amelia.cho@acme-payments.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-payments.com
Date: 2026-05-09T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: MSA / Order Form - liability cap and carve-outs

Hi Monica,

Thanks for the draft MSA and order form. Our legal team completed a first pass of redlines and has two main asks around Section 9 (Limitation of Liability) and consequential damages:

- Liability cap: We propose liability be capped at the greater of (a) fees paid in the prior 12 months, or (b) $500,000.
- Consequential damages: standard carve-out to exclude consequential, exemplary, and punitive damages, but include direct damages.
- Carve-outs: we ask that breaches of confidentiality, IP infringement, and wilful misconduct remain uncapped.

Attached is our mark-up (redlines_msa_v3.docx). We are trying to keep this within procurement’s standard risk tolerances given we will be processing cardholder-adjacent telemetry in production.

Timing: procurement is targeting signature by 2026-05-20. Please let me know if Redwood has flexibility on the cap language or if your legal needs more detail on the data handling carve-outs.

Best,
Amelia Cho
Sr. Counsel, Acme Payments
amelia.cho@acme-payments.com

Attachment: redlines_msa_v3.docx (MS Word, 284KB)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-05-09T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form - liability cap and carve-outs

Amelia — thanks for the redlines and the clear ask. Looping in Markus (legal) and Lauren (sales ops) to confirm risk appetite and commercial impact.

Quick thoughts from our side:
- We understand the request for prior-12-month fees as a sensible baseline. Our typical position for enterprise deals is cap = 12 months of fees OR 3x fees paid in the prior 12 months when there is elevated data risk, subject to a hard floor (e.g., $1M).
- For order forms with committed annual spend we sometimes offer an "annualized cap" (calculated per contract year) rather than a lifetime aggregate. That helps ongoing renewals and is sometimes acceptable to customers.
- Carve-outs: Redwood will not agree to completely uncapped exposure for IP claims or negligence; we usually accept carve-outs for wilful misconduct and gross negligence, and a limited carve for IP where indemnity terms limit the remedy.

Can Markus propose language we can share back? Lauren — can you confirm if this deal hits any reserved-discount bands we need to escalate?

I attached the current order form PDF for reference.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0178

From: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-09T18:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form - liability cap and carve-outs

Monica / Lauren — quick legal input.

We should aim for a negotiation band that protects Redwood while keeping the economics intact. Practical options (in order of preference):

1) Compromise A (preferred): Cap = the greater of (i) fees paid in the prior 12 months, or (ii) $1,000,000. Carve-outs: wilful misconduct and gross negligence remain uncapped; IP indemnity limited to costs of claim plus replacement or modification of infringing components (not punitive). Consequential damages excluded.

Rationale: $1M floor avoids disproportionate exposure on small ARR or pilots; keeps us in line with enterprise norms.

2) Compromise B (if customer insists on lower floor): Cap = 2x annual recurring fees (calculated per contract year) with carve-outs for confidentiality and IP (IP subject to indemnity limits).

3) Last resort (if procurement pushes): Cap = 1x prior 12 months fees, but add negotiated risk transfer (insurance confirmation + tighter SLAs + data security attestation).

Markus also recommends not to accept a lifetime cumulative cap that stacks across years without annual reset for long-running subscriptions — that can become unbounded relative to revenue.

I'll draft redline language for Section 9 and circulate.

-Markus
Markus Klein
General Counsel | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Cho <amelia.cho@acme-payments.com>
Cc: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-10T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form - liability cap and carve-outs

Amelia — appreciate the quick turnaround. Markus and I discussed and Redwood is prepared to propose the following compromise for your consideration:

Proposal (Redwood counter):
- Liability cap: greater of (a) fees paid to Redwood in the 12 months preceding the claim, or (b) $1,000,000; annual reset (calculated per contract year) for ongoing subscriptions.
- Consequential damages: excluded (standard).
- Carve-outs: wilful misconduct and gross negligence remain uncapped; IP claims handled via limited indemnity (costs of remedy and replacement/repair), not punitive damages.
- Data breach: limited to direct remediation and customer notification costs; we can agree to cooperation and reasonable assistance for investigations, but not open-ended consequential exposure.

We can provide redline language — will attach a tracked-changes MSA that implements the above. If you need the cap to be lower we’re open to a $750k floor but would need an insurance confirmation (cyber liability) and procurement acceptance of a 3-month remediation SLA for critical incidents.

Can you confirm which of the three options below is closest to Acme’s appetite so we can finalize:
A) Accept Redwood Proposal (1M floor + annual reset)
B) Counter with $750k floor + insurance confirmation
C) Keep 1x prior-12-month fees with no floor (will require additional mitigations)

Thanks — aiming to resolve before your signature target on 2026-05-20.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

Attachment: redlined_msa_redwood_proposal.docx (MS Word, 128KB)

Monica — thanks, appreciate the thoughtful compromise. Procurement and legal discussed and Acme’s preliminary position is: we prefer option C but can consider B if Redwood provides the specific insurance endorsement language and the tracked-changes MSA to review.

Action items from our side:
- We will circulate the redline back with specific edits to your proposed language by 2026-05-12.
- Please share the tracked-changes MSA (your attachment above) in editable format and include the cyber insurance confirmation text (carrier, limits, and endorsement).

If you can send the DocuSign link for the order form after we finish redlines, procurement will validate payment terms and expedite.

Best,
Amelia Cho
